newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Bucharest mayor chosen as Romania prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Bucharest mayor chosen as Romania prime minister.

text.p: The popular mayor of Bucharest was designated as Romania's future prime minister on Tuesday two days after reformist Emil Constantinescu won presidential elections, ousting former communists.

Officials of the Peasant Party (PNTCD), the largest party in a new parliament, told a news conference party leaders had chosen Victor Ciorbea to head the country's first coalition government not led by ex-communists.
Constantinescu, who turned 57 on Tuesday, is a member of the party and was certain to endorse the nomination. He will be sworn in next week.

Constantinescu ousted incumbent Ion Iliescu, a former communist who had led the country since 1989, in elections on Sunday. He has promised faster market reforms to improve some of eastern Europe's lowest living standards by blending tighter financial measures with increased pensions and benefits.
A no-nonsense trade unionist, Ciorbea became Bucharest mayor last June by beating Iliescu's handpicked candidate, former tennis star Ilie Nastase.
He has since embarked on an ambitious programme of cleaning up the capital, providing housing for young couples and free public transport for pensioners and students.

The Peasant Party won the most seats in this month's general elections as part of the Democratic Convention group headed by Constantinescu. It is to govern in a coalition with the Social Democrats, led by Former Prime Minister Petre Roman.
